The valence-6 plateau (about 2.6e-3) lives on the icosahedral mirror planes (base-edge arcs and base-face medians). The mixed Voronoi area converges on the same vertices, so their stars stay irregular (Voronoi cell different from A/3) under refinement; why is not derived (a kink of the recursive midpoint map across base edges is a plausible cause there, and no mechanism is given for the medians), and no closed form for the plateau is given. The off-mirror maximum stops decreasing near 4.5e-4 at level 7, so pointwise convergence off the planes is not established either.
The validators cannot tell whether raw bytes came from an instrument; the runner also requires a hardware probe in the task that cites them.
The witness heading difference comes from the two curvature profiles not being mirror images; the first-order kernels explain it only qualitatively
The workbench validator is exercised through the energy-accuracy kind; other kinds apply their own source parsers after the same canonical-base64 and byte-budget checks.
Thermal drift and probe lobing are not modelled.
Thresholds are relative and unitless; scans with very different scales may need other thresholds.
Tolerances are allocated half to lateral and half to heading error; other splits rescale every heading tolerance by the same factor and leave the first-order ranking unchanged.
Toolchain determinism (same inputs -> same bitstream) is not established
Tow width, compaction and tack are not modelled; tows are curves, not strips.
Traced geodesics are shortest paths only when no shorter corridor exists; not proved here.
Truth rotation rate is constant and known
Two geodesics only; resonant or chaotic geodesics are not sampled
Under the correct model a coasting track stays consistent (T069); the radius rule is a policy for model validity and data association, not a statistical necessity.
Unicode escape variants (\u0041 vs A) were not exercised.
Unit conversion follows one host convention (multiply by the factor); other conventions change which boundary samples collide.
Use time is on the same clock as the stamps
Validation recomputation (energy analysis) is counted separately from execution because it creates no occurrence and no result; the counterexample finding records it.
Variable-curvature paths add geodesic-position error to K(gamma(s)); its K-scaling is not separated here
Vendor SDK licensing and platform support were not checked
Vertex hits are refused rather than continued by the Polthier-Schmies angle-bisection rule.
Whether a reader of a forged workspace would be misled depends on how the record is displayed; not assessed.
Which part dominates is a property of the declared sigmas and noise model, not of any real scanner or sensor.
White common-mode error; a slowly varying common bias would defeat both filters and needs state augmentation.
White-noise acceleration is a modelling choice, not observed vehicle motion.
Witnesses show the statements are false in general; they do not rank routes for any application.
ciw.core.identities.canonical_json remains the ASCII variant because changing it would change every retained identity
created_at is a declared timestamp, not a trusted time.
kappa must be known along the path; estimating it from data is not modelled
q = 0.5 was chosen so the raw-R bias is visible per tick; smaller q shrinks tr(R^-1 H P- H^T) but never removes it.
sympy simplification is trusted to be correct; it is an independent implementation, not a proof checker

sympy.diffgeom assembles the connection and curvature only for seven surfaces; for gaussian-bump, gaussian-bump-shear and rotated-torus they come from ciw-written assembly of sympy derivatives, which is same-origin evidence.
uuid4 freshness is probabilistic, not enforced by a registry across workspaces.
w_bar and B are declared synthetic values; no physical disturbance was measured.
